policies.description: Only users with Administrator, Manager, or Agent roles may create a knowledge‑incident link; users with the Reporter role may not.
references: | **Administrator** (**admin**) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

| **Manager** (**manager**) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (**incident**, **problem**, **change**, **knowledge**); READ access to all the tables. Can **reassign** incidents/requests. Can **approve/reject** Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations. |

| **Agent** (**agent**) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | **Full CRUD** on **Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge**. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. |

| **Reporter** (**reporter**) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update **their own submitted Incidents/Requests**. Can search **Public Knowledge** articles. | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes. |

policies.description: Every knowledge‑incident link must record the `used_as` type, which must be one of the allowed values: suggested, applied, or resolution.
references: Search Policy: When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.
Use Tracking: All knowledge links must track used_as type: suggested, applied, or resolution.

policies.description: A knowledge article must be in the `published` state before it can be linked to an incident.
references: Article Status: Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.

policies.description: Before invoking the **link_knowledge_to_incident** tool, ensure that the `incident_id` refers to an existing incident (e.g., by calling **find_incident_by_id** or **find_incident_by_number**) and that the `knowledge_id` refers to an existing knowledge article (e.g., by calling **retrieve_knowledge_articles** or **find_incident_knowledge_links**). Only after both records are confirmed should the link be created; never fabricate or guess identifiers.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules. You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.

policies.description: When invoking the **link_knowledge_to_incident** tool, execute only that call in the current step. Do not combine it with any other tool calls or data‑modifying actions in the same request; if multiple links are needed, use an approved batch endpoint.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: All mandatory fields for the link operation (`incident_id` and `knowledge_id`) must be present and non‑empty before invoking the tool.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description:
When creating a new incident, first invoke the `retrieve_knowledge_articles` tool (or any equivalent knowledge‑search tool) using the incident’s short_description, category, impact, urgency, etc., as search criteria. For every knowledge article returned, call the `link_knowledge_to_incident` tool with the parameters:
- `incident_id`: the ID of the incident just created
- `knowledge_id`: the ID of the knowledge article to link
- `used_as`: set to the enum value `suggested`
The policy is met only if each call to `link_knowledge_to_incident` includes the `used_as` parameter with the exact value `suggested`.
references: • Search Policy: When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.
• Use Tracking: All knowledge links must track used_as type: suggested, applied, or resolution.

policies.description: Before creating a knowledge‑incident link, verify that the Incident and the Knowledge article belong to the same organization.

Before invoking the **link_knowledge_to_incident** tool, confirm that the authenticated user’s role permits the operation: 
- The user must have read (or higher) access to the target Incident (Agent, Manager, Administrator, or Reporter when the Incident was opened by that Reporter). 
- The user must be allowed to view the Knowledge article (any role can view a Knowledge article that is in the **published** state; only Agent, Manager, Administrator can link unpublished or internal articles). 
- If either check fails, abort the linking operation and return a policy‑violation error indicating the missing permission.
references: Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles.
Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes.
Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.
When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.

archive.description: For any matching article found during incident creation, the system must create an incident‑knowledge link with `used_as = suggested`.

archive.description:
**Audit logging for knowledge‑incident linking (self‑contained)**
When linking a knowledge article to an incident, the assistant must:
1. Invoke `link_knowledge_to_incident` with `knowledge_id` and `incident_id` (both non‑empty strings).
2. After a successful response, obtain the current UTC time (ISO‑8601) and the caller's user identifier (the `user_id` associated with the `x-itsm-user-token` supplied in the request headers).
3. Call `update_incident` on the same `incident_id` setting `worknotes` to a string formatted as:
   `[<ISO‑8601‑UTC‑timestamp>] Linked knowledge article <knowledge_id> to incident <incident_id> by user <user_id>`.
4. If step 3 fails, execute `remove_knowledge_link_to_incident` with the same `knowledge_id` and `incident_id` to revert the linking, and return the error to the requester.
All steps rely exclusively on the three tools listed in the API catalog; no external systems are required.
references: Time Tracking: All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.
archive.comments:
The policy is directly applicable to the knowledge‑to‑incident linking tool, so it is relevant and tool‑specific. However, the current set of supplied tools does not include any operation for creating or verifying work‑log entries, making it impossible to validate compliance before the link is made and to enforce the requirement using only the provided tool set. Consequently the policy is not actionable with the available tools and is not self‑contained; it relies on an external work‑log API that is not described. I propose an alternative, self‑contained description that explicitly names the required work‑log creation step and defines the rollback behavior if logging fails. Score: 2 – the policy is clear in intent but cannot be enforced or validated with the given tooling.
The policy is directly relevant to the `link_knowledge_to_incident` tool and is narrowly focused, so it scores well on relevance and tool specificity. However, it cannot be fully validated before the tool is called because the requirement to create a work‑log and potentially roll back the link depends on runtime outcomes. Moreover, the policy references a work‑log creation operation that is not defined in the supplied tool catalogue, and it assumes the existence of a rollback operation (`remove_knowledge_link_to_incident`) without describing its parameters. Consequently, the policy is not currently actionable or self‑contained with the available tools. To make it enforceable, the policy should explicitly name the work‑log tool, list its required parameters, and describe the rollback tool and its usage. Score: 2/5.
The policy is directly relevant to the `link_knowledge_to_incident` tool and is narrowly scoped, making it tool‑specific. Its intent can be validated: the required fields for the work‑log are known, and the error‑handling flow (undo on failure) can be checked after the operations. However, the policy references a `create_work_log` tool that is not present in the supplied tool catalog, rendering the policy not actionable with the current tool set and not self‑contained. To make it enforceable, either a description for `create_work_log` must be added to the tool list, or the policy should be rewritten to use an existing tool (e.g., `update_incident` with a work note) for audit logging. Overall clarity is good, but missing tool definition lowers practicality. Score: 3/5.
